To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) EML4-ALK–positive lung cancer cells become resistant to the ALK TKI crizotinig by developing gene amplification of EML4- ALK and/or a gatekeeper mutation (L1196M); (2) second-generation ALK inhibitors and the Hsp90 inhibitors 17-AAG are effective in treating EML4-alk–positive lung cancer that has become resistant to crizotanib.

crizotinibs are potent inhibitors of EML4-ALK–driven cancers but that cancers eventually develop resistance, and that second generation ALK inhibitors and Hsp90 inhibitors may be effective in treating these cancers.

crizotinig-resistant NSCLCs can be treated with either a next-generation ALK TKI or with an Hsp90 inhibitor, and that a unique PCR assay can be used to identify resistant cancers harboring the gatekeeping L1196M mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of resistance to ALK inhibition and the identification of alternative therapies to overcome resistance.
the molecular mechanisms that lead to resistance to ALK TKI therapy and how this resistance can be overcome.
the development of therapeutic strategies for the treatment of crizotimib-resistant EML4-ALK+ NSCLC.

crizotinibtreatment of patients with EML4-ALK-positive NSCLCs should be accompanied by close monitoring and early identification of resistance.
ALK TKIs are effective in treating NSCLCs harboring ALK translocations, but that cancers eventually acquire resistance to these inhibitors.
the EML4–ALK gene is a promising molecular target for lung cancer, but that the development of resistance is a major concern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the mechanisms of resistance to crizotine in EML4-ALK–driven lung cancer and that these mechanisms can be overcome with other ALK inhibitors and/or Hsp90 inhibitors.
the gatekeeper mutation is a major resistance mechanism to ALK inhibitors.
the ALK inhibitor crizotinob (PF-0231066) is effective in treating non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the fusion gene EML4-ALK.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gatekeeper mutation L1196M renders EML4-ALk resistant to crizotininib, but remains sensitive to the second generation ALK inhibitor NVP-TAE-684.
there are several therapeutic strategies that can be used to overcome resistance to ALK TKIs in patients with ALK fusion-positive NSCLC.
